chains.title: AP-2 family TF TFAP2E has a ref-favoring in vitro binding change, but occupancy and target regulation are unproven

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts that the ref allele binds an AP-2 model more strongly than the alt allele (effect -0.765, z -18.37), and TFAP2E has its own model with the highest HCT116 expression among the AP-2 candidates (8.5 TPM). However, TFAP2A and TFAP2C share the same mapped AP-2 model, and occupancy at this variant is unknown because no ENCODE ChIP-seq peak contains the site.

The variant is in a PYDC2-AS1 intron 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392, making it a candidate AP-2-responsive element, but no annotated cCRE directly overlaps the base and the dELS evidence is not HCT116-specific.
PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 19.5 kb and the variant lies within PYDC2-AS1, but there is no direct regulatory evidence linking this variant to PYDC2; GTEx reports no significant eQTL.
TFAP2E is expressed in HCT116 at 8.5 TPM, making an AP-2-mediated effect in this cell line plausible, but expression alone does not demonstrate TFAP2E activity at this element.

Open Targets reports no association between PYDC2 and colorectal cancer, and the cited literature does not directly establish a TFAP2E-PYDC2 colorectal cancer pathway; the phenotype link is speculative.

predictions: AP-2/TFAP2E ChIP or reporter assays should show stronger occupancy or activity for the ref T allele than the alt G allele.
